featured.oneLiner: An AI coding agent that runs entirely in a browser tab, with the model on the visitor's GPU and Python in a sandboxed worker, plus a benchmark of which harness features actually help a small model.
featured.theProblem: Small open models can run on a laptop for free but are weak at coding. The common fix is a better harness (plan, run, read errors, retry). The question was how much harness design can make up for a small model, and which parts of it actually help.
investigation: Ran everything in the browser: the model on WebGPU through WebLLM, and the code in a Pyodide worker with no network that gets killed and restarted if it hangs.

Built a v1 harness with 8 toggleable components, switched each off one at a time across a 40-task benchmark, and compared against fair baselines (the bare model, and the bare model with the same compute spent on retries).
Committed a 30-task held-out split before building harness v2, so v2 couldn't be tuned on it.
Plain retries beat both harnesses, so the public demo ships retries, with a replay mode for devices without WebGPU.

flow.label: Task
flow.detail: A Python function to write, with example tests. Hidden tests are kept back for grading.

flow.label: Model writes code
flow.detail: Qwen2.5-Coder, 4-bit, on the visitor's GPU via WebLLM and WebGPU.

flow.label: Sandbox runs it
flow.detail: Pyodide in a worker with no network. Hung code gets the worker killed and restarted.

flow.label: Examples pass?
flow.detail: No: sample again with a new seed. Yes: stop.

flow.label: Final grade
flow.detail: Scored on the hidden tests the agent never saw.

screenshots.alt: Pocket Agent solving a task live: three failed attempts, then a fourth that passes the example tests and all hidden tests.
Held-out pass rates: agent loop 57%, harness v2 77%, single attempt 67%, retry + check 87%.

verdict: On 30 held-out tasks (Qwen2.5-Coder 1.5B, 4-bit), retry-until-examples-pass reached 87% vs 57% for the full agent loop (9 wins, 0 losses, p = 0.004).
With the right harness the 1.5B model matched the 3B model at 87% and ran about 3x faster.
Removing any one of the 8 agent features changed the result by at most one task.
1,020 benchmark runs on an 8 GB MacBook; 70 tasks with 403 hidden tests; all raw results committed.

featured.codename: The Night the Star Left the Building
featured.oneLiner: Computer-use automation where an LLM works out a legacy back-office UI flow once, and a typed, reviewable artifact replays it deterministically with no model in the loop.
featured.theProblem: Banks and credit unions run a long tail of back-office apps with no API, where the only way in is to drive the UI like an operator. Calling a model on every run is slow, expensive and not reproducible.
investigation: Defined the capability artifact contract first (typed, parameterised, versioned JSON), then built a deliberately hostile target app with timeouts, 500s, interstitials and tenant skins to replay against.
Anchored reads on stable structure (row "Regular Shares" × column "Balance"), so a flow recorded for one member replays for any other. Ambiguous matches refuse instead of guessing.
Irreversible steps escalate: the run parks and a human takes over the same live browser session, and on resume replay skips any step the human already did.
Secrets are referenced by name only and never written to artifacts, logs or screenshots.

flow.label: Goal
flow.detail: A plain-English task on a legacy back-office app, e.g. read a member's balance.

flow.label: Discovery (once)
flow.detail: An LLM drives the real UI through Playwright, roughly 13 to 17 model turns.

flow.label: Capability artifact
flow.detail: Typed, parameterised, versioned JSON that a human reviews.

flow.label: Replay (every time)
flow.detail: Deterministic, no model, about half a second.
flow.note: stuck or risky? a human takes the live session

flow.label: Typed outputs
flow.detail: Success, a business outcome such as MEMBER_NOT_FOUND, or a clear failure.

verdict: 20 consecutive replays of alpha.member.balance: 20 successes, one distinct output, median 456 ms, worst 613 ms, zero model calls.
Discovery takes roughly 13 to 17 model turns once; every replay after that is model-free.
15 test files, including an assertion against the live app that an aborted transaction was never performed.

featured.codename: The Agent Who Was Handed Every Key
featured.oneLiner: A multi-agent customer-support desk on MCP where each agent's tool access is enforced at the tool boundary, not just requested in a prompt.
featured.theProblem: Most agent-with-tools systems give one model every tool and trust the system prompt to keep it in line. Support desks need billing, account and knowledge-base actions kept separate and auditable.
investigation: A LangGraph supervisor with zero tools routes each ticket to a billing, account or knowledge-base specialist. Each specialist owns its own MCP server, so other agents' tools never enter its prompt.
A call interceptor re-checks every request against one permission table, fails closed and writes denials to an audit log.
Built FailoverChatModel as a real chat-model class after a generic fallback wrapper silently dropped tools. It fails over only on rate limits, server errors and timeouts.

When both providers hit their daily caps mid-benchmark, the eval reported a confident but false result. The harness now separates provider errors from agent behaviour and refuses to publish a number it doesn't have.

flow.detail: Opened by the orchestrator on intake.

flow.label: Supervisor
flow.detail: Routes to billing, account or knowledge base. Holds zero tools.

flow.label: Specialist agent
flow.detail: Sees only its own MCP server, so other tools are never in its prompt.

flow.label: Interceptor
flow.detail: Re-checks every call against one permission table and fails closed.

flow.label: Resolve or escalate
flow.detail: Policy refusals come back with a hint; the graph hands off to a human.

verdict: Cut customer support resolution time by 38% with an MCP-powered multi-agent system that lets LLMs reach ticketing, billing and knowledge-base APIs through secure context sharing.
Increased automation coverage by 42% with FastAPI services and function calling, so agents handle password resets, refund requests and account lookups on their own.
75 tests passing, including one that gives the billing agent every server and asserts reset_password is still refused.

investigation: Built a scalable e-commerce platform with an AI outfit generator and personalized recommendations via Pinecone vector search and a fine-tuned Falcon 7B.

featured.codename: The Containers That Wouldn't Stay Dead
featured.oneLiner: A distributed Go/gRPC platform for deploying and running containerized services across a cluster, with Kafka event streaming and Kubernetes on AWS EKS.
featured.theProblem: Deploying containerized services across machines and keeping them healthy usually means adopting a heavy orchestrator. CloudFlow handles deployment, healing and load balancing with a smaller, purpose-built control plane.
investigation: Architected a distributed Go/gRPC backend with Kafka event streaming and PostgreSQL, defining content schemas and optimizing data flow.
Engineered scalable AWS EKS infrastructure via Kubernetes and CI/CD pipelines, with integrated observability tooling.
Split nodes into master (orchestration), builder (code to image, pushed to a registry) and worker (runs containers) roles.
Auto-heals dead containers, health-checks nodes, supports replicas, and load-balances on container health and stats.

verdict: Increased throughput by 30% by optimizing data flow.
Ensured 99.5% availability with EKS infrastructure and observability tooling.

featured.codename: The Witness Who Made Things Up
featured.oneLiner: A framework for evaluating vision-language and text LLMs on OCR and summarization, and for making their inference faster and more reliable.
featured.theProblem: Choosing a model family for document OCR and summarization means comparing accuracy, hallucination and throughput tradeoffs on real documents, not leaderboard numbers.
investigation: Evaluated vision-language and text LLMs in zero-shot and few-shot settings across OCR and summarization on 50K+ multimodal documents.
Optimized inference with vLLM, quantization and QLoRA.
Implemented LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation with DeepEval and RAGAS.
